column1: # Assumption Breaker Gate (ROADMAP O4a). Every claim in claims.tsv lists the assumptions its PASS rests on.

column3: assumption
column4: breaker: gate:<canary id in results.tsv, expect=fail>@<guard gate whose check the canary runs> | kcanary:<id in kani-canaries.tsv> | trusted:<why no breaker>

column1: # The guard must PASS on the real code in the same run, and the canary's recorded command signature must start with the
# guard's (claim-verdict.sh): the breaker is caught by the very check the claim relies on, not by an unrelated one.
# A breaker VIOLATES the assumption on purpose and must be caught for its reason; otherwise the claim FAILs.
# trusted:<reason> is allowed but printed with every PASS, so the reader sees what was not broken.

column3: the harness reaches both branches (not vacuous)
the harness calls the shipped function, so a bug in it is visible
no proof in the crate is silently skipped
the harness property is the intended behaviour (spec independent of the code)
column4: trusted:same author wrote spec and code; independent second spec pending (ROADMAP O4b)

column3: the harness judges the shipped body (no cfg(kani) fork)
the lint set fires on a planted panicking construct
code under test cannot rewrite the lint verdict
the forbidden lint set covers every panicking construct the crate uses
column4: trusted:NOT covered - assert!, slice::split_at, Vec::remove, Index::index(v, i) (round 3, finding A5); std calls trusted per their documented contract

column3: the code under test cannot switch a lint off with #[allow]
clippy judges the shipped body (no cfg(clippy) fork)
a sorry cannot pass the axiom audit
a false theorem fails the Lean build
every user theorem is mapped to a Rust test
the Lean model has the Rust semantics
the coverage gate fires below its threshold
the mutation gate fires on a surviving mutant
tests report their own outcome honestly (no early exit, no forged profile)
column4: trusted:tests are code under test (#39 item 3)

the tests judge the shipped body, not a cfg(test) variant
the tests check behaviour, not the source text (a source hash kills every mutant)
